questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Can anger and frustrate other drivers.
Cannot result in a traffic citation.
Reduces collisions by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can anger and frustrate other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe driving that can lead to aggressive behavior. You can receive a traffic ticket for tailgating.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination faster.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that tells you traffic laws. You must drive in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Before driving after snow, clear snow from your car's:
questions.explanation: Remove snow, ice, and frost from all windows so you can see clearly. Keep your headlights, brake lights, and taillights clean.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains when approaching railroad tracks. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop if:

options.text: The crossing lights are flashing red.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, or a flagger signals you to stop. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows where pedestrians cross. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to areas where bicycles, pedestrians, and animals may cross the road.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, alcohol's effects will only be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, check your rearview mirror for both headlights of the vehicle you passed. Only then is it safe to return to your original lane.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your body quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Only waiting will remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: You should not follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead stops suddenly, you may not have enough distance to stop and could crash.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: The best safety protection in a crash comes from:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Seat belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best with seat belts to protect you in front-end crashes. Always wear both.

questions.question: Alcohol and/or drugs affect which of these driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs reduce reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration. All of these skills are needed for safe driving.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn to get other drivers' attention.
Get out and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you stop on an interstate shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay inside your vehicle. Walking on an interstate is very dangerous due to fast-moving traffic.

questions.question: Alcohol:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Motor vehicle drivers should give children on bicycles extra space because:

options.text: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Children on bikes may suddenly ride onto the road from the sidewalk.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Park in a safe area and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park in a safe area and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of fatigue while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if you cannot keep your eyes open, drift from your lane, or need to turn up the radio and open windows to stay awake. If you notice these signs, find a safe place to park and rest.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger directs you to stop.
When a stop sign controls the crossing.
When flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: What should you do to ensure your health does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular medical checkups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, weakens your coordination, and impairs your vision. It makes it harder to judge distances and react to what is happening around you.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before driving on.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: You must always give pedestrians the right-of-way in the road, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver as they pass.
Speed up as they are passing you.

questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Avoid eye contact with them. Speeding up will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings if they obey traffic signals. Where there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in any crosswalk.

questions.question: Why are work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs used?

options.text: To frustrate drivers about slow traffic.
To keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones on highways are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests when entering a work zone.

questions.question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Fatigue while driving is as dangerous as driving drunk. Stop driving if you feel tired.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
The road will get narrower ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a dangerous hill or steep downgrade ahead. The hill may be very long or have sharp curves.
